name: Chinkhu
description: Chinkhu is a mountain in Nagaland, India.
facts: Listed in geographic records as a mountain in Nagaland
Included because mapped sites often stay off visitor itineraries

name: Kohima
description: Capital city of Nagaland and headquarters of Kohima district, perched on hills at about 1,444 m elevation. Main gateway and base for exploring Angami Naga culture, WWII history, and nearby valleys and peaks.
facts: Connected by road from Dimapur airport/rail (about 74 km)

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill in the heart of Kohima, commemorating the 1944 Battle of Kohima where Allied forces halted the Japanese advance. Features terraced graves of 1,420 Commonwealth soldiers, a tennis court outline from the fighting, and the famous epitaph.
facts: Site of the decisive 1944 Battle of Kohima
Maintained by Commonwealth War Graves Commission
Famous epitaph: for your tomorrow we gave our today

name: Dzukou Valley
description: High-altitude valley at about 2,438–2,452 m on the Nagaland-Manipur border, known as the Valley of Flowers of the Northeast for its seasonal wildflowers, rolling meadows of dwarf bamboo, and streams. Popular multi-day trek from Viswema or Jakhama.
facts: Famous for summer wildflowers and rhododendrons
Trek from Viswema or Jakhama villages

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village about 20 km west of Kohima, India’s first green village, with terraced paddy fields, traditional stone architecture, and the Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protecting Blyth’s tragopan. Model for community conservation and eco-tourism.
facts: India’s first green village (hunting banned since 1998)
Home to Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary
Homestays and guided cultural walks available

name: Japfu Peak (Mount Japfü)
description: Second-highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m in the Barail Range, about 15 km south of Kohima. Offers panoramic views, holds the Guinness record for the world’s tallest rhododendron tree, and is a popular moderate trek starting from Kigwema.
facts: Elevation 3,048 m, second highest in Nagaland
Trek from Kigwema village takes 4–5 hours
Best November to March for clear views and possible snow

name: Kisama Heritage Village (Naga Heritage Village)
description: Open-air cultural village 12 km south of Kohima between Kigwema and Phesama, designed as a traditional Naga settlement with morungs of all major tribes. Permanent venue of the annual Hornbill Festival in early December.
facts: Name derived from Kigwema and Phesama
Open-air living museum of Naga architecture

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State museum on Bayavü Hill in Kohima, established in 1970, displaying ethnographic collections of Naga tribal artefacts, costumes, weapons, textiles, wood carvings, and traditional structures across multiple galleries.
facts: On Bayavü Hill, about 1.5–2 km from centre
Galleries on ethnology, textiles, weapons, ornaments
Operated by Directorate of Art and Culture

name: Pulie Badze Wildlife Sanctuary
description: 9.23 km² wildlife sanctuary in Kohima district centred on the 2,296 m Pulie Badze peak overlooking Kohima. Established 1980, it protects habitats for Blyth’s tragopan and other birds and forms part of a larger highland biodiversity complex with Dzukou and Japfu.
facts: Named after legendary Pulie and the peak

name: Dzuleke Village
description: Small Angami Naga eco-tourism village in the Western hills of Kohima district, about 30–40 km from Kohima, known for community conservation, homestays, streams, forests, and ban on hunting. Model for sustainable rural tourism.
facts: About 30–40 km from Kohima via Khonoma
Hunting banned since 1999; eco-tourism board active
Homestays and trekking supported by NEIDA/Tata Trusts

name: Touphema Tourist Village
description: Community-run heritage tourist village about 36–41 km north of Kohima, recreating traditional Angami Naga architecture with cottages representing different khels (clans). Offers cultural immersion, local cuisine, and panoramic views.
facts: Model for rural tourism in Nagaland

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral (Kohima Cathedral)
description: Large Catholic cathedral on Aradura Hill in Kohima, blending traditional Naga house architecture with modern design. Consecrated in 1991, it features a 16-foot carved wooden crucifix and was partly funded as a memorial related to the Battle of Kohima.
facts: Largest cathedral in Northeast India by capacity
On Aradura Hill overlooking the city
